_readme: Star Chart question pools. Edit freely — no code changes needed. Each round mixes: 3 guess-the-fellow (generated from the fellows data), 3 'lore', 2 'places', 2 'realfake'. For 'lore' and 'places', 'answer' is the index into 'options' (options are shuffled on screen). For 'places' you can add a photo path (e.g. 'assets/quiz/quad.jpg') and it will show above the clue; leave null for text-only. For 'realfake', 'real': true/false and 'note' gives the truth.

lore.q: You've walked the whole Salthill prom. What's the ritual at the far end?
lore.note: Generations of Galwegians kick the wall at Blackrock before turning back.

lore.q: What river runs through Galway city?
lore.note: Short, fast, and full of swans — the Corrib.

lore.q: Galway's county colours, seen on every flag and jersey?
The Claddagh ring: the hands, the heart and the crown stand for…
lore.note: Born in the Claddagh, the old fishing village across the river.

lore.q: Galway is the City of the…
lore.note: Fourteen merchant families — the Tribes of Galway.
JFK Memorial Park — he spoke there in June 1963.

lore.q: Which company leads Galway's famous Halloween street parade?
The Spanish Arch was built in 1584 to…
options: Extend the city wall and protect the quays

lore.q: Which bridge do you stand on to watch salmon running upstream?
Our university opened its doors in 1849 as…
lore.note: Queen's College Galway → UCG → NUI Galway → University of Galway.

places.name: The Quadrangle
places.clue: Limestone, Tudor-Gothic, the oldest corner of campus — and the law says your graduation photo happens here.

places.name: James Hardiman Library
places.clue: Where this cohort's deadlines were actually survived. Silent floors, group-study rooms, the smell of stress.

places.name: The Spanish Arch
places.clue: Stone arches at the river's mouth where the whole city sits with chips the moment the sun appears.

places.name: Salthill Prom
places.clue: Two kilometres of seafront where half of Galway walks on a Sunday — diving tower included, swimmers optional, weather irrelevant.

places.name: Galway Cathedral
places.clue: The great green dome you can see from half the city — built on the site of the old jail.

places.name: The Long Walk
places.clue: The postcard: a single row of coloured houses along the harbour, photographed roughly nine million times a day.

places.name: Quay Street
places.clue: Cobbles, buskers, bunting and hen parties — the Latin Quarter street every visitor photographs first.

places.name: The Corrib walkway
places.clue: The riverside path from town up past the cathedral toward campus — swan escort included at no extra charge.

realfake.claim: "Craic" means fun, news and a good time, as in "any craic?"
"Giving out" means handing out free samples.
realfake.note: Giving out means scolding — as in "she was giving out to me all day."
It's the opposite — anyone from outside the city (Dubs would say all of Galway counts).

realfake.claim: "Fierce" means very — as in "fierce cold out."

realfake.note: A yoke is a thing — any thing — whose name you can't be bothered to remember.
Grand just means fine. Everything is grand. Even when it isn't.

realfake.claim: "Notions" means having ideas above your station.
